title: NDT Report Validation in Chicago, IL | Digital Data Review
description: Independent NDT report review for Chicagoland: refinery turnaround data, nuclear vendor records, power plant tube data and bridge weld UT, carried out remotely.
h1: Chicago-area NDT report validation for refineries, nuclear stations, power plants and steel structures
eyebrow: Report validation: Chicago and northern Illinois
intro: Northern Illinois combines nuclear stations, a major refinery in Will County, gas and coal-fired power plants, and a dense stock of steel bridges, viaducts and buildings, all inside one metropolitan economy. The inspection records they generate are read by plant inspection groups, utility engineers, bridge owners, insurers and lawyers, and each reader needs to know whether the report can carry the decision in front of them. We review Chicago-area NDT reports and the digital inspection data behind them independently, against the procedure and code that governed the work, and we do it remotely from the files you send.

highlights.h: City and state rules kept apart
highlights.p: Chicago inspects boilers and pressure vessels through its own bureau, while the rest of Illinois comes under the State Fire Marshal. The review notes which applied, so a record is never judged against the wrong jurisdiction.

Illinois certifies individual industrial radiographers as well as licensing the firms. For radiographs shot in the state, the review checks that the people named on the record held that certification when the exposures were made.

highlights.h: An opinion with nothing riding on it
highlights.p: We do not examine what we review, and the outcome makes no difference to us. That is what lets a contractor, an owner or an adviser put the written opinion in front of the other side.

p: Illinois regulates boilers and pressure vessels through the Office of the State Fire Marshal's Division of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety. Its state inspectors carry out every first inspection of new or used equipment, and inspectors employed by authorised insurance companies may carry out later inspections on the equipment they insure once it is registered.

The state act does not apply to boilers and pressure vessels in cities of more than 500,000 inhabitants, and inside the city limits Chicago has its own Boiler Inspection Bureau. City inspectors carry out internal inspections of high-pressure boilers and of low-pressure boilers used for processing, external inspections of boilers and unfired pressure vessels in operation, first inspections triggered by installation permits, and hydrostatic tests after installation or extensive repair. Repairs inside the city have to be made by a boiler repairer the City of Chicago licenses.

For a report review, the split matters in a simple way. A repair record from a plant in Cicero or Joliet and one from a building in the Loop may use the same ultrasonic technique, but they answer to different inspectors and different repair licensing. The opinion states which authority the equipment falls under and whether the NDT record gives that authority's inspector what it needs. It never stands in for the inspector: we do not act as an authorized inspector or as inspector of record anywhere.

ExxonMobil's Joliet refinery sits on about 1,400 acres in unincorporated Channahon Township, Will County, and has a capacity of 275,000 barrels a day, producing gasoline, diesel, liquefied petroleum gas, asphalt, sulfur and petroleum coke. Like every refinery, it generates inspection records in volume: API 510 vessel reports, API 570 piping surveys with their corrosion monitoring locations, API 653 tank records, exchanger tube data, and weld examination reports for repairs and alterations. Across the state line in Whiting, Indiana, BP's refinery adds to the regional volume; it has its own page in this section.

Reports of this kind reach us when an inspection group is closing out a turnaround and wants a second reader, when a contractor's report has been rejected and the contractor wants to know whether to argue or amend, and when someone acquiring or financing a downstream asset needs to know how far the inspection history can be trusted. In each case the seven checks are the same; what changes is the weight placed on each. A turnaround close-out concentrates on completeness and dispositions. A rejected report concentrates on the specific clause in dispute. Due diligence concentrates on whether data from different years and different contractors can be trended together.

sections.h: Nuclear stations southwest of the city and NRC Region III
p: Constellation operates six nuclear stations in Illinois: Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, LaSalle and Quad Cities, with Braidwood, Dresden and LaSalle in the counties southwest of Chicago. Federal oversight of all six comes from the NRC's Region III. Around the fleet sits a supply chain of fabricators, valve and pump shops and service contractors whose examination records end up in procurement packages and outage documentation.

We are not on any licensee's 10 CFR 50 Appendix B or NQA-1 approved supplier list, and nothing on this page should be read as a claim to be. What a licensee, a vendor or their counsel can get from us is an independent technical opinion, which the licensee's QA organisation then decides how to use. Requests of that kind usually concern non-safety-related scope, a vendor's records before a component ships, a disagreement between the plant's reviewers and a contractor's interpretation, or the technical facts in a commercial dispute.

Steam generator and heat exchanger eddy current data is often part of a nuclear package. Our Level III is not certified in eddy current, so for that data the proposal names a reviewer holding the certification the licensee's programme or the contract requires.

sections.h: Radiography in an Agreement State that certifies its radiographers
p: Illinois is an Agreement State, so the radiography firms working at Chicago-area plants and fabrication shops hold state licences rather than NRC ones. Illinois goes a step further than many states: under 32 Ill. Adm. Code Part 405, the Illinois Emergency Management Agency certifies the individuals who perform industrial radiography, in two categories, Certified Industrial Radiographer and Certified Industrial Radiographer Trainee, each with a class endorsement for radioactive materials, radiation machines or both.

That gives a Chicago radiography review an extra personnel check. Alongside the ASNT or employer certification that the code requires for interpreting the film, the reviewer looks for evidence that the people who made the exposures held the state certification appropriate to the source used on the dates in question, and that trainees were working under the supervision the rules expect. A missing state certification does not change what the image shows, but it can change whether the record is defensible.

Atlantis does not perform industrial radiography in Illinois or any other state. What we review is the product: film, computed radiography plates and digital detector images made by a licensed contractor, checked first for image quality and identification and only then for interpretation against the acceptance standard.

sections.h: Power plants, boilers and heat recovery steam generators
p: Gas-fired and remaining coal-fired units around Chicago produce outage records that look different from refinery ones. Boiler tube thickness surveys, waterwall and superheater tube sample reports, header and high-energy piping weld examinations, and HRSG tube data dominate. The construction codes are ASME Section I for boiler external piping and the boiler proper and ASME B31.1 for power piping, with the National Board Inspection Code governing repairs.

The reviewer's questions follow the damage. For tube thickness surveys: were readings taken at the locations where wastage or erosion actually occurs, and can they be trended against the last outage? For weld examinations on alloy piping: was the examination done after the final heat treatment, was hardness or alloy verification recorded where the specification required it, and do the ultrasonic records show coverage of the full weld volume? For HRSG tubes: was access good enough for the technique claimed? The opinion separates paperwork gaps from examinations that could not have found the damage that matters.

sections.h: Movable bridges, viaducts and high-rise steel
p: The Chicago Department of Transportation is responsible for more than 300 bridge and viaduct structures, including 37 operable movable bridges along the Chicago and Calumet Rivers, and works under a signed preservation agreement covering the movable spans. Rehabilitation of those structures, of viaducts and of the state's highway bridges produces weld inspection records to AASHTO/AWS D1.5, while building steel and industrial structures are examined to AWS D1.1.

Bridge ultrasonics carries a specific technical question. The Federal Highway Administration's December 2024 memorandum, based on NCHRP research, warns that some modern plate carries sound at a different velocity from the calibration block and can be acoustically anisotropic, which can mislocate indications or weaken the reflected signal. It recommends contract special provisions requiring velocity measurements and limiting search angles. Where a Chicago-area contract includes them, the review checks that the report records the measurements and respects the limits; where it does not, the opinion notes whether the plate type makes the question relevant.

For building and industrial steel, the review typically examines ultrasonic reports on complete joint penetration welds in moment connections and magnetic particle reports on fillet welds and repairs. Common findings include calibration blocks that are not identified, scanning patterns that miss part of the weld, and discontinuities recorded without the length and location needed to judge them against the code's acceptance table.

p: The seven checks run on every report. Northern Illinois adds a few questions of its own, which the table sets out.

p: Chicago-area contractors now deliver most of their work as digital inspection data: DR images in DICONDE or proprietary formats, encoded phased array and TOFD files from fabrication and outage work, eddy current tube data from exchangers and steam generators, and corrosion maps from refinery piping. Owners receive the final report through digital reporting platforms, often signed electronically and loaded directly into an inspection database or a computerised maintenance system.

A review of digital inspection data checks what the PDF cannot show. The reviewer opens the native files, confirms that each one belongs to the weld or component the report lists, re-gates or re-measures the indications behind the dispositions, and compares the instrument settings stored in the file with the procedure. For the digital reporting step, the review checks template revision, the identity and authority of each electronic signature, the time stamps against the dates of work, and whether any fields were carried over from a previous report. Data that survives those checks can go into the owner's systems with confidence; data that fails them is identified before it shapes an interval or a repair plan.

sections.h: How the review runs without a Chicago desk
p: No Atlantis employee, office or facility exists in Chicago or anywhere in Illinois. The company works from Houston and Hyderabad, and Chicago-area reviews are carried out remotely, entirely on the reports, images and raw files that clients send through a secure transfer.

To start, send the report or a sample of the package with the procedure, the code and a line on what the review is for. We reply within one business day, setting out a review scope and a quote. The review then applies seven checks to each report: procedure compliance, personnel qualification on the date of work, equipment and calibration, technique adequacy, acceptance criteria, interpretation and sizing, and completeness and traceability.

An ASNT NDT Level III with certification in ultrasonic, radiographic, magnetic particle, penetrant and visual testing leads the review of records in those methods. For anything else, the proposal names a reviewer holding the certification the work requires. The review team as a whole brings experience from nuclear, maritime, oil and gas and petrochemical work.

Each report is given one of three verdicts. Sound: the record supports what it concludes. Deficient in documentation only: the examination looks adequate, but the paperwork has gaps that can be closed without new work. Deficient in disposition: the evidence cannot carry the accept or reject decision, and the component needs engineering attention or re-examination.

faqs.q: Does it matter whether our equipment is inside the City of Chicago?
faqs.a: It matters for who inspects it. The city's Boiler Inspection Bureau covers boilers and pressure vessels inside city limits; the State Fire Marshal's division covers the rest of Illinois. The review checks the NDT record against what the relevant inspector will expect.

faqs.q: Can you review radiographs from an Illinois radiography contractor?
faqs.a: Yes, as a document review. We check image quality, identification and interpretation, and look for evidence that the radiographers held Illinois industrial radiographer certification on the exposure dates.

faqs.q: Do you work with Illinois nuclear stations?
faqs.a: We provide independent technical opinions that a licensee or vendor may use as its QA organisation decides. We are not on any licensee's Appendix B or NQA-1 approved supplier list.

faqs.q: Can you check bridge weld ultrasonic reports for a Chicago-area project?
faqs.a: Yes. The review covers calibration, scanning, sizing and acceptance against AASHTO/AWS D1.5, plus any velocity and angle provisions the contract adds following the FHWA memorandum.

faqs.q: Do you review refinery turnaround packages from Will County?
faqs.a: Yes. Vessel, piping, tank and exchanger records are reviewed against API 510, 570 and 653 and the owner's procedures, as batches during the outage or as a close-out review.

faqs.q: Who reviews eddy current data from power or nuclear plants?
faqs.a: A reviewer holding the eddy current certification your contract or programme requires, named in the proposal. Our Level III's certification is limited to UT, RT, MT, PT and VT.

faqs.q: Will the review tell us the remaining life of our equipment?
faqs.a: No. Remaining life and fitness-for-service under API 579 stay with your engineer. The review tells the engineer whether the measurements underneath that calculation are reliable.

faqs.q: Do you come to site in Chicago?
faqs.a: No. Reviews are done remotely from the files you send. If something the review needs is missing, the opinion lists it so the contractor can supply it.
